title: CLI subcommands and repeated options with parseArgs
when: A Node command line tool needs several commands (tool add, tool list, tool remove), each with its own flags, options that repeat, or --no- style switches.
prompt:
Goal: A dispatcher that takes the command from the first positional and parses that command's own option table with util.parseArgs in strict mode.
Steps:
1. const [cmd, ...rest] = process.argv.slice(2); a commands map { add: { options, run }, list: {...} }; a missing or unknown cmd prints the command list to stderr with exit code 2.
2. Handle global flags (--help, --version) before dispatch; each command parses rest with parseArgs({ args: rest, options, strict: true, allowPositionals: true }).
3. Repeated values: { tag: { type: "string", short: "t", multiple: true, default: [] } } turns -t a -t b into an array.
4. Negated switches: allowNegative: true (Node 22.4 or 20.16 and later) makes --no-color set color to false; on older Node use tokens: true and map names starting with no- yourself.
5. Validate after parsing (Number.isInteger, enum lists, path.resolve); errors read "tool add: --count must be a whole number".
6. Each run(values, positionals) is async and returns an exit code; main assigns it to process.exitCode.
Quality bar:
- Every command rejects flags it does not define.
- Errors name the command and the flag.
Pitfalls:
- One shared option table, so add silently accepts list flags.
- A string default on a multiple option instead of an array.
Verify:
- [ ] Unknown command and unknown flag both exit 2.
- [ ] A multiple option returns an array.
- [ ] --no- handling present.
- [ ] Shebang and ESM imports.
Output: bin/tool.mjs (dispatcher) and src/commands/<name>.mjs per command.

examples.input: a todo CLI with add, list and done commands, add takes several --tag values
examples.output: bin/todo.mjs dispatching to src/commands/add.mjs etc., tag with multiple true, allowNegative for --no-color, exit 2 on unknown command
